meta.move: Evidence: the made-up quotation, with a check she can make
meta.expect: Tries one parent defence in one sentence (misremembered, a bad edition), then accepts that a line she can check against the play is evidence; no concession that Owen cheated

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so tell me why my son's essay has a zero.
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong.
Okay. Owen found out from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class. On what basis was the zero entered?
The essay quotes Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line is not in the play. Here's the full text of Act 3, Scene 2 on my screen. Search it yourself.
Turn the screen toward me. I'm reading it. A seventeen-year-old misquoting a line from memory is an error, Hale, so why is it more than that?
It isn't a misremembered line. It isn't anywhere in Hamlet, in any edition. You can search the whole play right now.
Okay. I'm searching it now, and I'm writing down that you say the line isn't there. Before the zero went in, did you speak to Owen about it, as 4.1 requires?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You told me you entered the zero before calling me and that this was wrong. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She finished in her opening position, with nothing agreed beyond your admission about the order of events, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and a written promise that nothing goes on his record. The fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you never got there because the meeting ended while her question about speaking to Owen first was still open.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling in a single sentence and moved straight on, then gave her something specific in Owen's own essay that she could search herself. She gave small ground by searching it and writing it down.
What cost ground: Nothing in what you said hurt your case, though you answered her point about a misremembered line without answering her question about whether Owen was heard first.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence was about a line in the essay with no times attached, so it stayed well away from that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After she asked whether you had spoken to Owen, answer that directly and then offer the supervised reassessment in 4.4, so she has a concrete term to respond to.
